Understanding

What is a Migraine?

A migraine is a neurological condition that causes intense, throbbing head pain, usually on one side. Unlike common tension headaches, migraines often present with associated symptoms like severe nausea, vomiting, and extreme sensitivity to light, sound, and smell.

An attack can last from several hours to days, making daily activities impossible. Our targeted diagnostic and therapy framework aims to reduce the severity and frequency of your migraine episodes using cutting-edge medical treatments.

Neurological Basis
Involves brain chemicals & nerves
Aura Phase
Visual cues in 25% of cases
Hereditary Aspect
Family history is common
Modern Therapies
CGRP inhibitors and Botox work
Recognition

Types of Migraines

Migraines are classified depending on the presence of sensory warning signs called auras.

Migraine with Aura

Preceded by visual flashes, blind spots, tingling in hands/face, or temporary speech issues about 10-60 minutes before the headache begins.

Visual Aura Sensory Warning

Migraine without Aura

The most common type. Severe, throbbing, one-sided pain occurs without prior warning signs, lasting 4-72 hours if left untreated.

Common Type Pulsating Pain

Chronic Migraine

Diagnosed when headaches occur on 15 or more days a month for at least 3 months, with at least 8 of those days presenting as typical migraines.

Severe Pattern Daily Impact

When to Seek Emergency Care

Seek immediate medical attention if your symptoms include:

Sudden, explosive "thunderclap" headache
Headache with high fever and stiff neck
Numbness, paralysis, or weakness on one side
Double vision or difficulty speaking
Recognition

Symptoms & Warning Signs

Migraine symptoms occur in stages, ranging from early fatigue (prodrome) to sensory aura, the painful attack, and post-attack exhaustion (postdrome).

Key Symptoms
  • Throbbing, pulsing pain
  • Severe nausea/vomiting
  • Sensitivity to light & sound
  • Worse with movement
Sensory Disturbances
  • Flashing lines in vision
  • Blind spots/scotomas
  • Numbness or tingling
  • Temporary slurred speech
Postdrome "Migraine Hangover"

After the severe pain subsides, patients often experience extreme fatigue, brain fog, and muscle aches lasting up to 24 hours.

Diagnosis

Diagnosing Migraines

We combine historical symptom tracking with diagnostic imaging to identify the specific migraine type and formulate a tailored care plan.

1

Detailed History

Mapping pain frequency, location, duration, family history, and associated triggers like stress or diet.

2

Neurological Exam

Checking reflexes, eye movements, sensation, cranial nerve responses, and coordination.

3

Brain MRI

Advanced imaging scans to rule out secondary headache causes, structural issues, or vascular abnormalities.

4

Trigger Mapping

Creating a digital diary tracking lifestyle patterns, hormonal cycles, sleep quality, and diet to narrow triggers.

Treatment

Comprehensive Migraine Treatments

We combine modern rescue therapies with long-term prophylaxis to desensitize nerve pathways and reduce migraine burden.

Acute Rescue Medications

Stop migraine attacks in progress

Taken immediately when an attack starts, these medications help stop the throbbing pain, sensory sensitivity, and nausea.

  • Triptans and Ditans
  • CGRP receptor antagonists (gepants)

Preventive Treatment

Reduce attack frequency & severity

For patients with frequent attacks, daily oral medications or monthly injections help prevent the brain from launching a migraine episode.

  • Beta-blockers, anticonvulsants, or antidepressants
  • Monoclonal antibody CGRP blocker injections

Botox Injections

FDA-approved chronic migraine relief

Botox injections administered every 12 weeks around the head and neck block pain transmitters, providing substantial relief for chronic migraine.

  • Targeted muscle injections
  • Blocks chronic pain pathway receptors

Lifestyle & Wellness

Holistic support & trigger mapping

Proper hydration, consistent sleep schedules, stress reduction, and healthy nutrition are critical to reducing migraine triggers.

  • Sleep hygiene & hydration tracking
  • Dietary trigger identification

FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

Answers to common questions regarding migraine types, triggers, and relief treatments.

A headache causes general pain in the head or neck area, while a migraine is a complex neurological disorder. Migraines cause throbbing, pulse-like pain (typically on one side), often accompanied by sensory sensitivities (light, sound, smell), severe nausea, or visual auras.

Common triggers vary but include hormonal fluctuations, stress, skipped meals, dehydration, lack of sleep, sensory stimuli (bright lights, loud noises), changes in weather, and certain foods or beverages (such as caffeine or aged cheeses).

While there is currently no cure for migraines, modern therapies (such as Botox, CGRP injections, and oral preventive medications) can dramatically reduce the frequency, duration, and severity of attacks, allowing most sufferers to live completely pain-free lives.
